subject: Subsetting a plot and overlaying subset (plot zoom within plot limits)

messages.author: c196cceefa902bfc
messages.subject: Subsetting a plot and overlaying subset (plot zoom within plot limits)
parts:
Hi,

 I have a series of lines plotting individuals against species richness (species-accumulation curves) that I am comparing to some literature values. Some of the literature values only go up to a very small number of individuals and I would like to subset the part of the whole plot that more clearly displays these curves and then overlay the resulting subset within the whole plot limits. I've attached a crude plot to that effect but I would like to know how to achieve it in ggplot2.

Any thoughts appreciated - please just point me in the direction of useful functions

Thanks

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Subsetting a plot and overlaying subset (plot zoom within plot limits)
parts:
Basically you're going to need to dive into the world of grid::viewport, functions that "create viewports, which describe rectangular regions on a graphics device and define a number of coordinate systems within those regions." There's a nice example of doing so here:

http://learnr.wordpress.com/2009/05/08/ggplot2-plot-inside-a-plot/

...and I'm sure other places on the web as well.

Ben
